title: Transition-of-Care Requests in Prior Authorization
content:
A new member of Prairie Ridge Health Plan can ask that a service already authorized by the prior health plan be honored under Prior Authorization.

## Continuity of care clauses

**Clause 1: the request.** A new member whose prior health plan authorized a service may ask, inside the transition period, for that authorization to be honored, and Prairie Ridge records a transition-of-care request built on the member's earlier Prairie Ridge approval for the same service code, whose units requested carried over the units the prior plan's authorization had left; the request takes that approval's class, providers and service code, is received and starts on the day it is recorded, and waits for the prior plan's authorization number where the class requires it.

**Clause 2: when the units are fixed.** The units a transition-of-care request asks for are fixed only after every earlier approval of the member for the same service code whose end date has passed carries an expiry release entry.

Clause 2 read the other way round: while any earlier approval of the member for that service code has an end date in the past and carries no expiry release entry, the units of the transition-of-care request are not yet fixed.

| Element of the request | What it is |
|---|---|
| Basis | the member's earlier Prairie Ridge approval for the same service code |
| Class, providers, service code | taken from that earlier approval |
| Received date and start date | the day the request is recorded |
| Prior plan's authorization number | awaited where the class requires it |
| Status once recorded | submitted |

## Tool reference: `record_transition_of_care_request_bf098d50`

### Situation of use and capability
The tool records a new member's transition-of-care request with Prairie Ridge, a request that the authorization the member's prior health plan had given be honored here. One call opens one new Prior Authorization request, received today and starting today, marked as arising from transition of care and reviewed on the standard timeframe, for the service code and the number of units given. It takes its authorization class, therapy discipline, requesting provider, servicing provider and network status from the member's earlier Prairie Ridge authorization named as its source, and it carries no prior-plan authorization number until one is supplied. The new request is visible at once in the member's list of prior authorizations with status submitted and its own authorization number.

### How it is invoked
`record_transition_of_care_request_bf098d50` is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks it and then calls it.

### Parameters
- `customer_id`: the member reference number of the member the request is for, as returned by the member profile lookup (an identifier).
- `membership_id`: the reference number of the member's Prairie Ridge plan membership the request falls under, as returned by the plan membership lookup (an identifier).
- `source_authorization_id`: the reference number of the member's earlier Prairie Ridge prior authorization for the same service, from which the class and providers are taken, as returned by the prior authorization lookup for the member (an identifier).
- `service_code`: the CPT or HCPCS service code of the service to be honored, copied character for character exactly as it appears on the member's earlier Prairie Ridge authorization for that service, with no change of letters, digits or spacing.
- `units_requested`: the number of units the transition-of-care request asks to honor, in the authorization class's unit basis, written as whole integer units.

### Return
A confirmation sentence stating the new request's reference (an identifier beginning with "auth_"), its authorization number (text of the form PA-YYMM-NNNNNN), its status (submitted), the date received (YYYY-MM-DD, today) and the whole number of units requested. The presence of the new reference and authorization number shows that the request was recorded. The tool defines no other return.
